plan: [This is a second-price auction with common value and a strong winner’s-curse risk. My private signal is low (14). In common-value settings bidders should shade below naive estimates; truthful bidding is not safe. With no history to learn from and a single round, I avoid overbidding and limit downside by not exceeding my perceived value. I will bid my private perceived value (conservative, no positive information about others), which avoids likely negative expected payoff from the winner’s curse.]

[I compute the posterior for the common value given my signal v=43. Feasible common values are integers 23–29 (since noise ∈[-20,20]), equally likely, so E[common|v]=average(23..29)=26. In a second-price auction with common-value signals, bidding my conditional expected common value mitigates the winner's curse. Therefore I will bid $26.00 to maximize long-run expected profit given this signal. ]

[The common value C is uniform 20–29, and private noise is uniform so my signal (39) gives no update; E[C]=24.5. In a second-price auction the profit-maximizing long-run strategy is to bid my expected common value to avoid the winner’s curse. Bidding 24.5 (allowed by $0.1 increments) is the rational, risk-neutral choice here. ]
